target.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation
target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR2/6 in the durable-core series and the first implementation slice.
It is stacked conceptually after the docs-only architecture gate in #107375.

GitHub cannot use a fork-only PR1 head as the base of an upstream PR, so this
submission is cumulative against `release/2026.7.1`. The implementation-only
delta is available in the [PR1-to-PR2 compare](https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/openclaw-durable-release-head-pr1-rfc-20260714...codex/durable-core-pr2-storage-v2):
21 files, 7,358 additions, and 8 deletions. The cumulative upstream surface is
25 files, 7,887 additions, and 8 deletions.

## What Problem This Solves

Official 7.1 has durable owner-specific tables but no optional shared boundary
for generic execution evidence, wake obligations, delivery-attempt evidence,
uncertainty, correlations, and bounded payload references. This slice adds
only that residual storage while preserving existing owner authority and
leaving disabled installations untouched.

## Exact base and head

- Official base: `release/2026.7.1` at
  `0790d9f593ad30c940ed93b5872a8cf6d6f3cf8c`.
- PR1 RFC head included in this cumulative branch:
  `5b8dfa9aade`.
- Exact PR2 head: `ee7b9194a528e261efe80bba199fd780d9d4b407`.
- The head is a direct descendant of the exact official base; no 7.1
  correction commit is reverted.

## What this slice adds

- An opt-in durable configuration boundary.
- An enabled-only schema inside the existing shared `openclaw.sqlite` owner.
- A typed SQLite/Kysely store with explicit transaction composition.
- Read-only schema opening and fail-closed future-version preflight.
- Shared database handle/lease lifecycle that preserves existing state owners.
- Generated Kysely types plus naming and raw-SQL guardrails.

This PR does not start a worker, integrate agent front doors, dispatch a wake,
expose Gateway/CLI methods, or claim external delivery. Those are later gated
slices.

## Owner-first schema decision

Existing official 7.1 owners remain authoritative: `task_runs`,
`task_delivery_state`, `flow_runs`, `subagent_runs`,
`delivery_queue_entries`, `state_leases`, session/ACP/restart owners, audit,
and diagnostics.

When durable runtime is enabled, this slice adds exactly ten residual tables:

1. `durable_execution_records`
2. `durable_event_evidence`
3. `durable_execution_steps`
4. `durable_payload_refs`
5. `durable_run_correlations`
6. `durable_timer_obligations`
7. `durable_signal_evidence`
8. `wake_obligations`
9. `delivery_attempt_evidence`
10. `uncertainty_facts`

There is no second migration ledger, mode table, result-mailbox table, generic
dedupe ledger, cleanup table, or duplicated task/flow/subagent lifecycle. The
existing `schema_meta` owner receives one `durable_runtime` version row.

## Safety properties proved

- Disabled configuration creates no database, WAL, SHM, schema metadata, or
  durable table.
- Read-only inspection never creates or migrates state.
- A future durable schema version fails before DDL, metadata updates, or
  backfill.
- Enabled initialization upgrades a real official 7.1 shared database while
  preserving canonical owner rows, including an existing `state_leases` row.
- Durable writes can join a caller-composed shared SQLite transaction and roll
  back atomically.
- Shared handles remain open while another lease is active, do not checkpoint
  prematurely, and reopen cleanly after final close.
- Terminal mutation guards, source-owner/ref requirements, dedupe keys, bounded
  metadata, and lease fencing are enforced by the store.
- Raw SQLite remains limited to explicit schema/bootstrap and store-lifecycle
  boundaries; JSON extraction uses a closed-path Kysely helper.

## Evidence

Run on `ee7b9194a528e261efe80bba199fd780d9d4b407`:

- `pnpm tsgo:all` - passed across all workspace projects.
- `pnpm vitest run src/durable/config.test.ts src/durable/sqlite-store.test.ts src/durable/store-factory.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.permissions.test.ts src/state/sqlite-query-plan.test.ts` - 6 files passed; 58 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` - generated schema/types match.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` - Kysely guardrails OK.
- `pnpm check:durable-canonical-naming` - passed across 27 files.
- Scoped type-aware oxlint over every changed script/config/store source - passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` - passed on all matched changed files.
- `pnpm docs:map:check` - passed for the cumulative RFC docs.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

The focused matrix includes enabled/disabled initialization, exact table
inventory, canonical-row preservation, future-version rejection, transaction
rollback, terminal immutability, wake claim fencing, close/reopen persistence,
shared-handle lifecycle, query plans, and the closed JSON-path no-silence
diagnostic regression.

## Review and stack gate

- #107375 remains the architecture/RFC gate.
- #110143 is closed and superseded; this branch does not reuse its broad schema
  or runtime boundary.
- The five beta3 proof PRs remain untouched as archives.
- PR3 will not be submitted until both PR1 and this PR reach at least
  `rating: platinum hermit`. Later branches already exist on the fork only so
  their ancestry and proof can be prepared without bypassing that gate.

## Non-claims

- No default-on durable behavior.
- No claim that storage alone prevents every silent agent outcome.
- No arbitrary semantic replay or exactly-once external side effect.
- No public mutation API and no claim that queue acceptance proves user
  delivery.
